inline_comments.comment: The `MaskedMTKNPT.__init__` calls `MolecularDynamics.__init__` directly, bypassing `MTKNPT.__init__`, and then reproduces all of `MTKNPT`'s initialization logic verbatim (thermostat creation, barostat creation, `_temperature_K`, `_pressure_au`, `_kT`, `_q`, `_p`, `_h`). This is a significant code duplication: any future change to `MTKNPT.__init__` (e.g. adding a new state variable or validation) must be manually reflected in `MaskedMTKNPT.__init__` too, with no compile-time safety net. A better design would expose an override point in `MTKNPT.__init__` — for example, a `_init_cell_momenta()` template method — so `MaskedMTKNPT` can call `super().__init__()` and only override the parts that differ (cell momentum initialisation). This is especially important because `_integrate_q`, `_integrate_p`, and `_integrate_q_cell` are inherited from `MTKNPT` and all read `self._p_g`, so the parent and child must stay in sync on all state variables.

Per project convention, `get_conserved_energy()` must use `atoms.get_potential_energy(force_consistent=True)` plus kinetic energy computed from momenta, rather than `atoms.get_total_energy()`. Using `get_total_energy()` can produce inconsistent energies for certain calculators (e.g. ones where the energy is not force-consistent by default), breaking the apparent conservation. `NoseHooverChainNVT` and `IsotropicMTKNPT` in the same file both use `get_potential_energy(force_consistent=True) + get_kinetic_energy()` correctly; the new `MaskedMTKNPT.get_conserved_energy` should match that pattern.

`self._h0_basis` is computed once at initialisation from the initial cell `self._h` and never updated during MD steps. Because cell vectors evolve during NPT dynamics, the fluctuation direction unit vectors become stale as the simulation proceeds. Whether this is intentional (fix the axis directions to the initial lattice orientation) or an oversight should be determined and, if intentional, documented explicitly. For large cell deformations — which are precisely what NPT enables — using fixed initial basis vectors can introduce systematic drift in the axis-projected forces computed in `_integrate_p_cell`.

The `_p_g` property reconstructs the 3×3 matrix using a Python list comprehension fed into `np.sum([...], axis=0)`. This creates a temporary Python list of three (3×3) arrays before the summation, which is slower than a vectorised approach. The equivalent one-liner `(self._p_c * self._h0_basis.T) @ self._h0_basis` avoids the intermediate list and the `np.sum` call entirely. Additionally, placing the trailing comma before `axis=0` on a line by itself (`, ` at the start of a line) is non-standard formatting that may confuse readers.

The `_p_g.setter` raises `AttributeError()` with no message. If this setter is ever triggered unexpectedly — for example, if a future subclass forgets to override a parent method that assigns to `_p_g` — the resulting `AttributeError` will give no indication of why it fired or what the correct alternative is. Raising `AttributeError("_p_g is read-only in MaskedMTKNPT; update self._p_c directly")` makes the invariant self-documenting and aids debugging.

`self._cell_dof = 9 if mask is None else sum(mask)` gives `cell_dof = 0` when `mask=(False, False, False)`. This propagates to `self._R[0] = 0 * kT * pdamp**2 = 0.0`, which then causes a division-by-zero in `_integrate_xi` (`self._xi[j] += delta * self._p_xi[j] / self._R[j]` for `j=0`). A guard should be added: `if mask is not None and not any(mask): raise ValueError("At least one mask entry must be True")`. An all-False mask is physically equivalent to NVT and should use `NoseHooverChainNVT` instead.

The public method `integrate_nhc_baro` has its first positional parameter renamed from `p_g` to `p_cell`. `MTKBarostat` is directly importable and used in the test suite, so any caller that was using the keyword-argument form (`barostat.integrate_nhc_baro(p_g=..., delta=...)`) will now get a `TypeError`. This rename is semantically appropriate (the parameter is now used for both a 3×3 matrix and a 3-vector), but it is a backward-incompatible API change and should be noted in the changelog.

The test now parametrises `test_anisotropic_barostat` over mask configurations (including `(True, False, False)` and `(True, True, False)`) while the barostat input `p_g` is still initialised as a 3×3 matrix (`rng.standard_normal((3, 3))`). When `MaskedMTKNPT` uses `MTKBarostat` it passes `self._p_c`, a 3-vector with inactive elements set to zero. The round-trip test (time-reversal symmetry) holds for any input shape because the NHC chain merely scales the input, but the kinetic force term `np.sum(p_cell**2) / W` sums all 9 elements of the 3×3 matrix while `cell_dof = sum(mask)` only counts the active axes — so the equilibrium condition is not being exercised in the way the masked barostat is actually used in production. Each masked test case should use a 1D input array of length `sum(mask)` to match the production call path through `MaskedMTKNPT._integrate_p_cell_by_barostat`.

`test_masked_npt` checks energy conservation and that positions change, but never verifies that the mask is actually enforced. The core correctness guarantee of `MaskedMTKNPT` is that masked-off cell dimensions remain fixed. For example, with `mask=(False, False, True)` the a-length and b-length should be constant throughout the run. Without an assertion such as `assert np.isclose(np.linalg.norm(md._h[0]), initial_a_length)` for each masked-off axis, a bug that silently ignores the mask entirely would still pass this test.

The entry reads `Add \`MaskedMTKNPT\`\`` — note the unmatched double backtick at the end, which is a reStructuredText syntax error. The class name should also use a proper Sphinx cross-reference per project convention: `:class:\`~ase.md.nose_hoover_chain.MaskedMTKNPT\``. Additionally, the description only mentions NPzT; since the class also supports NPxT, NPyT, and biaxial variants, consider broadening the description to something like "cell fluctuations along user-specified crystallographic axes (e.g. NPzT)".

general_comments.comment: The `MaskedMTKNPT.get_conserved_energy` method is nearly identical to `MTKNPT.get_conserved_energy`, differing only in the cell kinetic energy term (`np.sum(self._p_c**2)` vs `np.sum(self._p_g**2)`). If `MTKNPT.get_conserved_energy` were refactored to delegate the cell kinetic energy calculation to an overridable helper method (e.g., `_get_cell_kinetic_energy()`), then `MaskedMTKNPT` would only need to override that single helper and could remove its entire `get_conserved_energy` override. This would also make the conserved quantity formula consistent between the two classes and reduce the surface area for future divergence.

The inherited `MTKNPT._integrate_q`, `_integrate_p`, and `_integrate_q_cell` methods all call `np.linalg.eigh(self._p_g)` to diagonalise the cell momentum matrix. For `MaskedMTKNPT`, `_p_g` is a rank-deficient matrix (sum of outer products for active axes only). For HCP cells (the test fixture), the lattice vectors are orthogonal in the relevant subspace and this works correctly. For general non-orthogonal cells, the eigenvectors of `_p_g` will mix cell directions, potentially introducing unintended changes to the cell shape of masked-off axes. This edge case should be documented, or a check added that warns when the active mask axes are not mutually orthogonal.

The diff shows `doc/ase/md.rst` is not modified, meaning `MaskedMTKNPT` would not appear in the generated documentation. Per project convention, new MD integrator classes must be registered in `doc/ase/md.rst` with an `.. autoclass::` directive under an appropriate section heading. Without this, users have no way to discover the new class through the official documentation.
